subject: gov.policy
name: Digital Egypt service-coverage targets
milestone: 242 services now, over 270 by end-2026, about 450 by 2030
position_start: The platform was in operation; the base's last count before the window is more than 170 e-government services (2024-09-30), and no target series is on record
position_end: The minister set out 242 services at 2026-07-21, a target of over 270 by end-2026 and about 450 by 2030, under a legislation and governance pillar alongside digital transformation, technology localisation, digital infrastructure and capacity building

subject: gov.policy
name: ICT 2030 strategy and the digital government programme
milestone: 105 entities connected and 242 services live, July 2026
position_start: The ICT 2030 strategy on three pillars of digital transformation, digital skills and jobs, and technological innovation, with the digital platform at 210 services and 10.7 million users at the start of 2026
position_end: A cabinet follow-up meeting recorded 105 government entities connected electronically and 242 services available on the national platform. The ministry names data as a main transformation platform and linking government digital systems as the strategic objective, and reports a 47-place improvement in an international ranking

subject: gov.policy
name: National Artificial Intelligence Strategy, second edition, the document

subject: gov.policy
name: National Cybersecurity Strategy
milestone: Third edition under preparation, stated to the Senate
position_start: The base carries no dated statement of which edition was in force at 2025-08-01, or of the strategy's content
position_end: The second edition is being implemented through projects to protect digital infrastructure and build cyber defences, and a third edition is being prepared; the national emergency readiness centre is being developed to use AI against cyber threats
note: No edition dates, text or publication is held; the whole position rests on one ministerial statement to a Senate committee

subject: gov.policy
name: National data-centre strategy
milestone: Preparation confirmed on presidential directive
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: Under preparation, framed around data localisation, a regional storage and processing hub, digital sovereignty and digital-services exports, and reaffirmed by Cabinet on 2026-07-05 and by the minister on 2026-07-21; no publication date, draft text or governing instrument is held
note: The ministry says data-centre licensing continues to expand in the meantime

subject: gov.policy
name: National Digital Health Strategy
milestone: Launched November 2025
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: Launched in November 2025 on secure, interoperable systems and data-driven decision-making, and carried forward in the FY2026/27 economic and social development plan, which targets expanded use of artificial intelligence in health - diagnostic support, predictive models built on electronic health records, precision medicine and drug-research efficiency - and calls for specialised health datasets carrying the professional terminology used in diagnosis
note: the strategy text itself is not on file; the plan is reported rather than held

subject: gov.policy
name: National Spectrum Strategy 2026-2030 and the 410 MHz award
milestone: US$3.5bn agreement signed with the four operators
position_start: Did not exist; the strategy's period begins in 2026
position_end: 410 MHz of additional spectrum awarded across 1.8 GHz, 2.6 GHz and 3.5 GHz, doubling operator holdings in a single transaction, for US$3.5bn paid by the operators to the regulator; the minister stated the award matches all spectrum allocated in Egypt over the previous 30 years
note: The strategy document itself is not held. Egypt refarmed 2.6 GHz for 5G rather than licensing dedicated mid-band, and set no coverage or speed obligations comparable to its neighbours'

subject: gov.legislate
name: Bills amending the information technology crimes law
milestone: Two separately sponsored bills submitted, April 2026
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: One bill would strengthen protection of children against newly emerging electronic crimes; a second, separately sponsored, would address artificial-intelligence-generated deepfakes and tie fines to the benefit obtained. Both are private members' bills with no passage recorded

subject: gov.legislate
name: Child national ID card proposal
milestone: Two workshops held on the proposal
position_start: Not on record
position_end: A member's proposal for a national identity card for children carrying a photograph from age five, requiring amendment of the Child Law, discussed at two workshops; recommendations included a unified national child-data platform, a full biometric identification system for children, and linkage between health, education and other government databases. No bill has been tabled
note: Participants also recommended a strict legal framework for protecting the resulting personal data

subject: gov.legislate
name: Cybercrime Law 175 of 2018 and its enforcement record

subject: gov.legislate
name: Digital space bill
milestone: Draft described by its sponsor 2026-08-10
position_end: A 54-article, seven-chapter party draft that would require digital platforms to appoint a legal representative in the country and register influencers on a national platform, and would regulate the use of artificial intelligence, deepfakes, online extortion, gambling and child protection online; not tabled, and no text is published
note: the article count and the preparation time are the sponsoring member's own account; it is separate from the cabinet's social-media legislative review

subject: gov.legislate
name: Electronic service of judicial notices
milestone: Cooperation protocol signed at the Supreme Judicial Council's headquarters
position_start: Not on record
position_end: The postal service's digital postbox becomes the official platform for electronic delivery of judicial notices to individuals, companies and institutions, bound to the user's national identification number and carrying identity verification, electronic signatures and seals, encryption, delivery timestamps and correspondence tracking, so that a registered electronic message has the same legal validity as registered paper mail
note: The protocol text is not held; the position for people without an account and the treatment of failed delivery are not stated

subject: gov.legislate
name: Executive Regulations 816 of 2025, the instrument itself

subject: gov.legislate
name: Financial Regulatory Authority technology sandbox
milestone: Two projects approved 2026-09-01
position_start: The base carries no position on the sandbox at 2025-08-01; the authority states that 2026-08 closes its first year
position_end: preliminary approval granted to two further financial technology projects to enter the sandbox
note: The sandbox's opening date and establishing decision are not held; the first-year figures are the authority's own

subject: gov.legislate
name: Freedom of information bills
milestone: Syndicate-backed bill submitted with 60 signatures, August 2026
position_start: No freedom of information statute
position_end: A syndicate-backed bill submitted after securing 60 lawmakers' signatures would create an authority for the protection of freedom of information; a separate member's bill was submitted the day before with its text carried in the reporting, and the minister of state for information told the prime minister in July 2026 that coordination was under way to issue the law quickly. Nothing is enacted

subject: gov.legislate
name: Licensing framework for data centres and cloud services
milestone: Framework issued under the telecommunications law, August 2021
position_start: Not held
position_end: The regulator's licensing and registration framework for establishing and operating data centres and providing hosting and cloud computing services - the operative rule beneath the country's data-centre estate

subject: gov.legislate
name: National register of personal-data use, proposal
milestone: Proposed in Parliament 24 August 2026
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: A member proposed on 24 August 2026 a national register letting citizens see which bodies have obtained or processed their personal data and why, on a secure platform logging onward sharing, with instant alerts where data is suspected of being used to open an account, mobile line or e-wallet, binding deadlines for handling misuse complaints and remediation costs borne by the offending body, and a data-minimisation rule; he cited mobile lines registered on citizens' data without their knowledge and a school taking loans in parents' names, and argued the 2020 data-protection law needs enforcement rather than replacement
note: a member's proposal, with no bill text or government response on file

subject: gov.legislate
name: PDPL Executive Regulations, Decree 816 of 2025
milestone: Issued by ministerial decree 2025-11-01, circulated December 2025
position_start: Did not exist. The Alexandria Economic Court decided the Orange Egypt case in February 2025 on tort grounds precisely because the regulations were still pending, more than four years after the law passed
position_end: In force, establishing the approvals model, a separate licence for each cross-border transfer specifying destination, purpose, data categories and safeguards, extra approvals for electronic marketing and certain public-space surveillance, registered data-protection officers, and breach notification within 72 hours to the regulator and three business days to affected individuals
sources: 2026-02-11 Egypt finalises Executive Regulations to the PDPL (Decree 816-2025)|2025-09-02 Egyptian court judgment tightens data-protection enforcement (Orange Egypt)
note: The Regulations' own text is not held; the base carries two law-firm summaries of it

subject: gov.legislate
name: Property ID Law
status: Implemented, implementing decree not on record
milestone: Approved by the House of Representatives 2025-04-27
position_start: Approved by the House, having been introduced in August 2023; it mandates a unique digital ID for every property recording location, use, ownership, licensing, violations and transaction history, tied to a unified digital base map, and makes the property ID a prerequisite for registry or notary registration and for utility connections
position_end: Unchanged; no prime-ministerial decree naming the overseeing authority, no executive regulations and no commencement date are on record fifteen months later
sources: 2025-05-14 Egypt approves Property ID Law to digitise real estate|2026-07-20-youm7-pm-census-2027-implementation
note: Tampering carries EGP 5,000-30,000 fines or up to six months' imprisonment; national-security properties are exempt

subject: gov.legislate
name: Real property register conversion, Manshah section, Sohag
milestone: Deferred to 2027-07-01
position_start: The title register was due to take effect for the Manshah city survey section on 2026-07-01 under a decision of 2000
position_end: Deferred by one year to 2027-07-01 by a justice ministry decision published in the Official Gazette, with settlement forms admitted for that section for two months from 2026-07-01 to complete the legal procedures
sources: 2026-08-04-egypt-justice-minister-delays-real-estate-registry-sohag|2016-06-14 Securing Land Tenure in Egypt - Who Needs Registered Titles (Sims, Metropolitiques)
note: Egypt's move from deed registration to a title-based cadastre proceeds survey section by survey section under a 1964 statute; no national completion figure is held

subject: gov.legislate
name: Regulator unit monitoring AI-manipulated social-media content
milestone: Existence disclosed to Cabinet
position_start: Not on record
position_end: The ICT minister told Cabinet that a unit had been formed inside the telecommunications regulator which already detects and acts on AI-manipulated video and imagery, but that legislative amendment is needed to address the practices at root
note: The unit's formation date, legal basis, staffing, method, appeal route and contest procedure are not stated; the detection capability operates ahead of the instrument that would authorise it

subject: gov.legislate
name: Regulatory framework for cybersecurity services
milestone: Framework issued by the telecom regulator, June 2024
position_start: Not held
position_end: The regulator's operative framework for providing cybersecurity services, resting on the 2018 information technology crimes law and the 2003 telecommunications regulation law; the regulator separately signed a framework agreement on cross-border cyber security cooperation with a Gulf cybersecurity council in October 2025

subject: gov.legislate
name: Regulatory framework for foreign satellite operators
milestone: Entered into force 2024-07-09, adopted 2023-10-08 with a grace period
position_start: In force since 2024-07-09, the standing licensing instrument for any foreign satellite operator serving earth-station terminals in Egypt, granting categorical licences to operators supplying space capacity to licensed providers
position_end: Unchanged; no foreign low-earth-orbit operator has been licensed under it
note: The telecommunications law criminalises unlicensed wireless equipment with a minimum of one year's imprisonment and a fine of EGP 20,000-50,000

subject: gov.legislate
name: Social-media legislative review
milestone: Cabinet agreed a legislative review 2026-07-29
position_start: Not on record; the base holds no proposal to amend the social-media statutes before 2026-07-29
position_end: A cabinet meeting chaired by the Prime Minister agreed on a review of the governing statutes, heavier financial penalties and public awareness campaigns; the ICT minister said a comparative study of other states' approaches is being prepared. No bill, text or timetable is stated
note: The Prime Minister credited a press and media campaign with prompting the government's response

subject: gov.legislate
name: Standalone digital-privacy statute proposal
milestone: Demand put on the parliamentary record
position_start: No standalone digital-privacy bill on record
position_end: A member called on the government to bring forward a comprehensive digital-privacy bill criminalising recording and publication without consent, imposing takedown duties on platforms, raising penalties where fake accounts, defamation, extortion or vulnerable victims are involved, and widening investigators' powers to trace anonymous accounts
note: The demand does not reference Law 151 of 2020 at any point - a parliamentarian arguing for a privacy statute as though the country had none

subject: gov.legislate
name: Statistics and census law 35 of 1960
milestone: High committee for the 2027 census convened by the prime minister, February 2026
position_start: The 1960 statute vesting censuses and statistics in a technical body constituted by presidential decree, published by the statistics agency under its own heading of the laws regulating statistical work
position_end: The statute is unchanged and the machinery under it moved: the prime minister chaired the high committee for the 2027 population, housing and establishments census with the agency and six ministers, and a national statistics strategy had been in preparation for nearly two years with 18 ministries and research bodies plus international partners

subject: gov.protect
name: Data-protection compliance guidelines and templates
milestone: Published January-February 2026
position_start: Did not exist; no regulator guidance is recorded in the base before 2026
position_end: Ten guidelines published, covering consent, lawful bases of processing, electronic direct marketing, the data protection officer, officer categories, data users, principles, records of processing activities, licences and permits, and privacy notices, together with breach-notification and records templates
sources: 2026-06-23 Bimonthly Update on Privacy in Africa (January & February 2026)
note: The digest dates the guidelines only to January-February 2026, so the day is padded

subject: gov.protect
name: Data-protection enforcement actions
milestone: One judgment on record
position_start: One award on record: the Alexandria Economic Court ordered an operator to pay EGP 10 million in February 2025, on facts from November 2022, after an unconsented SIM replacement
position_end: The same single judgment. The base records no regulator decision, fine, registration figure or cross-border-transfer licence issued at any date to 2026-08-06
sources: 2025-09-02 Egyptian court judgment tightens data-protection enforcement (Orange Egypt)
note: The judgment rests on tort and custodian's liability, not on the data-protection law, so it is not regulator enforcement

subject: gov.protect
name: Data-protection regulator enforcement and licensing record

subject: gov.protect
name: Face-print collection for mobile line registration
milestone: Four mobile operators referred to the public prosecutor, 10 August 2026
position_start: Identity verification for a mobile line without published biometric collection
position_end: The regulator referred all four mobile operators to the public prosecutor over lines registered in subscribers' names without their knowledge, and took regulatory measures alongside the referral
note: the first enforcement against operators over subscriber registration the base holds; no penalty, prosecution outcome or affected-line count is published

subject: gov.protect
name: Personal Data Protection Center
milestone: Confirmed as supervisory authority by the Executive Regulations
position_start: The base carries no dated statement of the Centre's standing, staffing or activity at 2025-08-01; its first appearance in this section's source base is 2025-11-16
position_end: Confirmed as the body implementing, monitoring and enforcing the law, running the approvals and cross-border-transfer licensing regime, officer registration and breach receipt; the acting chief executive framed data sovereignty as a strategic necessity at a November 2025 workshop
sources: 2026-02-11 Egypt finalises Executive Regulations to the PDPL (Decree 816-2025)|2025-11-16-egypt-data-sovereignty-pdpc-cairo-ict-ahram

subject: gov.protect
name: Personal Data Protection Law 151 of 2020
milestone: Executive Regulations issued 2025-11-01
position_start: In force since 2020 but never operationalised, with no executive regulations issued
position_end: Operationalised by the Executive Regulations; the law's obligations on purpose limitation, approvals, cross-border transfer licensing, data-protection officer appointment, 72-hour breach notification and guardian consent for under-15s become enforceable from 2026-11-01 at the end of a one-year grace period
sources: 2026-02-11 Egypt finalises Executive Regulations to the PDPL (Decree 816-2025)|2025-09-02 Egyptian court judgment tightens data-protection enforcement (Orange Egypt)|2025-06-21 Regulating Privacy and Digital Identities in the Age of AI - the View from Egypt (Cairo Review)
note: The statute's provisions are structural; the commencement of enforcement is the dated fact

subject: gov.protect
name: Prosecution referral over lines registered without consent
milestone: All four mobile operators referred to the Public Prosecution, 2026-08-23
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: The regulator has referred all four mobile operators to the Public Prosecution over lines registered in users’ names without their knowledge; no charge, hearing date or penalty is on file
note: Reported inside the regulator’s half-year complaints report rather than as a separate enforcement notice.

subject: gov.regional
name: Chairmanship of the Arab AI governance and quantum working groups
milestone: Elected chair of two of six working groups
position_start: Did not exist. The Arab Permanent Committee for AI and Emerging Technologies was created by a ministerial resolution at a session Egypt hosted in January 2026 and held its first founding meeting in May 2026
position_end: Egypt chairs the AI Governance Working Group, whose remit is a guidance framework for AI governance, technical tools and mechanisms for activating the Arab Charter for AI Ethics, and the Quantum Computing Working Group, whose remit is an Arab quantum strategy and quantum-cybersecurity deployment
note: The committee is mandated to propose regional agreements and coordinate a unified Arab position, a bloc track running alongside rather than through the continental AI work

subject: gov.regional
name: Council of Arab Ministers of Communications and Information
milestone: 29th session hosted in Cairo, 22 January 2026
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: The 29th session, hosted by the communications ministry in Cairo, approved the establishment of a regional committee for artificial intelligence and emerging technologies and adopted a regional charter on artificial-intelligence ethics as a guiding and advisory document rather than a binding instrument

subject: gov.regional
name: Cross-border personal data transfer regime
milestone: Executive regulations issued by decision 816 of 2025
position_start: Cross-border transfer governed by the 2020 personal data protection law
position_end: The executive regulations set the conditions, procedures and fees for a licence or permit to transfer personal data across borders, for legal and natural persons alike - five years after the law provided for them

subject: gov.regional
name: Egypt's position on the AU Malabo Convention

subject: gov.regional
name: UN E-Government Development Index position
milestone: 2024 index published
position_start: 95th of 193 with a score of 0.6699 on the 2024 index, inside the global top 100 but below Egypt's 2010 peak of 86th
position_end: The same 2024 figure; no later reading is held at 2026-08-06
sources: 2024-09-23 South Africa, Mauritius and Tunisia Lead E-Government Progress in Africa (UN EGDI 2024)|2025-07-14 Between Ambition and Implementation - Egypt's e-government experience (Masaar)
note: A named analyst argues the index's three pillars omit legislative and administrative frameworks, equality of access and protection of fundamental rights

subject: gov.standards
name: National standards body and the international-standard default
milestone: Smart-metering data-exchange standard endorsed, 2025
position_start: The standards organisation as the sole official body for preparing and issuing national standards, founded by presidential decree in 1957
position_end: A 2022 ministerial decision provides that where no national standard exists, an international or foreign standard applies, from a named list. The register carries a 2025 national standard adopting the international smart-metering data-exchange standard, giving electricity metering a common exchange basis

subject: gov.standards
name: Sustainable Finance Taxonomy
milestone: Inter-ministerial working group formed 2026-08-07
position_start: Not held
position_end: Under development by an inter-ministerial working group formed by the central bank with the finance, investment, environment and financial-regulatory authorities, ahead of official issuance
note: no draft text, reporting obligation, data requirement or issuance date is stated

subject: gov.standards
name: Transfer-pricing guidance
milestone: No update since 2018
position_start: The approved guide dates from 2018 and has not been revised despite successive changes to the legislation and to international standards
position_end: Unchanged. The chair of a chamber of commerce tax committee told a financial daily the file needs urgent intervention, and appeal committees have begun relying on statutory provisions requiring a minister-approved guide, with the result that some transfer-pricing penalties have been cancelled
note: Attributed throughout to named practitioners, not to the tax authority

subject: gov.discourse
name: Citizen participation and the complaints channel
milestone: Monthly report to the prime minister for September 2025
position_start: An electronic participation index of 0.5890, ranked 74 of 193 in the 2024 survey
position_end: The unified government complaints system received 195,000 complaints, appeals, requests and enquiries in September 2025, of which 153,000 were routed to competent bodies. Against that, an international assessment scores the country 14 of 25 on obstacles to access, 9 of 35 on limits on content and 5 of 40 on violations of user rights

subject: gov.discourse
name: Council of State digital transformation plan
milestone: Stated as under way, no deliverable named
position_start: The base carries no record that the administrative-justice branch had a digitisation programme
position_end: The head of the Council of State told a meeting of administrative-court circuit presidents that the Council continues to implement an integrated digital transformation plan, developing its information infrastructure and adopting current technology to speed litigation; no named system, date, figure or deliverable is stated
note: The only first-hand record the base has that this branch has a digitisation programme at all

subject: gov.discourse
name: Public consultation on the data-protection Executive Regulations

subject: gov.discourse
name: Regulatory public consultation framework
milestone: Framework issued by the telecom regulator, June 2021
position_start: Not held
position_end: A bilingual framework issued by the telecom regulator for public consultations - the only published mechanism the base holds for non-governmental input into a regulatory decision. No consultation held under it, and no response document, is recorded

subject: gov.discourse
name: VAT credit-refund period reduction
milestone: Awaiting completion of legislative steps
position_start: The base carries no earlier statement of the refund period or of the proposal
position_end: A proposed cut of the credit-refund period to four months for taxpayers and three for small and medium enterprises is still awaiting its legislative steps; a tax association board member added that the reduction will not meet its objects unless the operational problems obstructing proof of balances are resolved first
note: Offered against a comparator of a neighbouring state refunding within 12 to 24 hours

subject: finance.budget
name: Budget allocation for data centres and state AI
milestone: Communications ministry document reported 2026-08-21
position_start: None published
position_end: An intended allocation of up to US$860 million a year from the general budget, from FY2026/27 to the end of 2030, for data centres, computing infrastructure, data security and privacy, and artificial-intelligence use inside state-owned companies, on a stated target of 0.10-0.15 per cent of GDP
note: an intention on a ministry document relayed at second hand; no appropriation line, and the country's operating data-centre count is a commercial directory's rather than the state's

subject: finance.budget
name: Economic and Social Development Plan FY2026/2027

subject: finance.budget
name: ICT sector public investment
milestone: FY2025/26 plan presented to the House of Representatives
position_start: Not held
position_end: EGP 13bn of public investment allocated to the communications and information technology sector in the 2025/26 plan, against plan targets of US$8.5bn in annual digital exports of which US$6bn from outsourcing
note: a plan allocation presented to parliament, not an outturn; no execution figure against it is held

subject: finance.budget
name: Startup Charter EGP 50bn financing initiative, appropriation and disbursement

subject: finance.budget
name: State appropriation for digital transformation and for the ICT ministry

subject: finance.mou
name: Central bank cooperation with Eswatini
milestone: Governors' meeting reported; event date not stated
position_start: The base carries no dated position on the relationship at 2025-08-01, though prior cooperation on capital standards, financial inclusion, small-business finance and climate-related risk is described
position_end: Eswatini seeking to draw on Egypt's continental payment-system accession experience, with Egypt also offering its currency-circulation system, its currency printing house and banking institute training programmes
note: Neither source states the meeting date, so the event date is unestablished; no instrument was signed

subject: finance.mou
name: Central bank memorandum with Afreximbank on a pan-African Gold Bank
milestone: Memorandum of understanding signed
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: At feasibility-study stage, to assess technical, commercial and regulatory requirements for a Gold Bank sited in a designated free zone in Egypt, scoped to include an internationally accredited refinery, secure vaulting and associated financial and trading services
note: Egypt is the lender's largest shareholder and its host; siting is subject to the study and subsequent approvals

subject: finance.mou
name: Fawry point-of-sale integration partnership
milestone: Partnership signing announced
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: An integration connecting the payments company's acceptance terminals with a point-of-sale software provider's system, targeting hospitality, retail chains and hypermarkets
note: No sums, merchant counts or transaction volumes are disclosed

subject: finance.mou
name: Memorandum on a regional IT outsourcing delivery centre
milestone: Memorandum of understanding signed with the IT industry agency
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: A framework for expanding the firm's operations in Egypt and establishing a regional outsourcing delivery centre serving Middle East and North Africa clients in business consulting, risk management, cybersecurity, digital engineering, data analytics, AI and business platforms, stated as creating more than 1,000 jobs over three years
note: No investment sum, no site and no opening date are stated; the job figure is the company's and the agency's

subject: finance.new
name: Blnk consumer lending facility
milestone: US$37.1m raise announced
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: US$12.5m Series A equity led by a domestic venture fund with three development and regional investors, plus US$24.6m in local-currency debt from three Egyptian banks, against a point-of-sale lending network of more than 3,000 merchants
note: The company stated that around 75% of its clients had never borrowed in the formal market

subject: finance.new
name: Development partner financing of digital and transport infrastructure
milestone: Youth credit line loan to a payments company, April 2026
position_start: A US$200m partial guarantee for sustainable transport and digital infrastructure, and a health insurance loan of 2020
position_end: A development bank lent up to EGP 250m, about EUR 4.4m, to a payments company's small-business finance arm under a youth credit line with European cash incentives of up to 10% of the loan amount. The transport and digital infrastructure guarantee's monitoring report records formal consent in October 2025 to use bond proceeds for revised eligible subprojects

subject: finance.new
name: Egypt Startup Charter and unified financing initiative
milestone: First Startup Label Certificates issued, one recipient named
position_start: A government framework in preparation, with a stated unified financing initiative of EGP 50bn to support 5,000 startups and help 500 of them attract more than US$1m each, against targets of US$5bn in investment over five years and 500,000 jobs; no launch, appropriation, disbursement or governing instrument on file (2025-12-19)
position_end: The Startup Label certification is issuing under the Charter: UMAMI E-Learning Solutions named as one of the first Egyptian companies awarded the Startup Label Certificate, assessed on innovation, technological reliance, scalability and investment readiness; no cumulative certification count, and no appropriation or disbursement figure for the stated EGP 50bn financing initiative, is held
note: Certification criteria are as UMAMI and the ministry report them, company-reported; no appropriation or disbursement record for the financing initiative accompanies it

subject: finance.new
name: Fawry revenue and market capitalisation
milestone: Market capitalisation of EGP 67.72bn reported
position_start: No 2024 figures are on file; the source states market capitalisation had nearly doubled over the previous year
position_end: 2025 revenue of EGP 8.65bn and net revenue of EGP 3.1bn; market capitalisation of EGP 67.72bn, given by the source as about US$1.3bn at April 2026, with about six million transactions processed daily
note: Egypt's second-largest listed fintech by market capitalisation after the state-owned payments company; source is paywalled

subject: finance.new
name: Hassan Allam Digital Infrastructure data-centre licence
milestone: Regulator licence granted, reported 2026-06-16
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: Licence to build and operate a data centre, developed with a technology partner, backed by a stated initial US$400m first-phase investment and described by the regulator as the tenth data-centre licence issued in two years; no site, capacity in MW or opening date stated
note: The source gives the licence date as Monday, May 15 with no year, and 2026-05-15 was not a Monday, so either the day or the weekday is wrong in the source

subject: finance.new
name: Sale of a majority stake in the Regional Data Center Hub
milestone: Telecom Egypt board withdrew from the agreement
position_start: Did not exist at 2025-08-01; the agreement was announced 2025-09-07
position_end: Cancelled for unmet conditions, with the buyer having been due 75-80% of the unit; the hub is instead to be carved out as a wholly-owned subsidiary with its own technical and commercial team
note: Consideration and the specific unmet conditions are not disclosed; the stated reason is transactional, not sovereigntist

subject: finance.new
name: Sinai hyperscale data centre proposal
milestone: Proposal put to the investment and foreign trade minister
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: Targeted investment approaching US$1bn, starting at 10,000 sq m with an expansion vision to 500,000 sq m, seawater cooling, and power wholly from the consortium's green hydrogen and solar project; the minister required a full feasibility, financing structure and shareholder file, and coordination with three ministries and security bodies
note: Talks, not a project; no site, licence, financial close or date is stated

subject: finance.new
name: State telecom infrastructure investment since 2019
milestone: Figure stated to the Prime Minister
position_start: No cumulative investment figure is on file at 2025-08-01
position_end: More than US$6bn invested in telecom infrastructure since 2019, with about 3,000 new towers planned in-year, more than 9,000 over three years and a stated target of 40,000 towers by 2028
note: Stated in US dollars by the ministry; the currency of account and the split between state and operator spending are not given

subject: infra.connect
name: 2Africa Egyptian landing stations and ready-for-service dates

subject: infra.connect
name: 2Africa submarine cable, Egypt transit and Mediterranean segment
milestone: Mediterranean capacity activated on the Port Said-Genoa-Marseille route
position_start: Mediterranean capacity in service since January 2025, with Egypt a transit hub rather than a terminal landing
position_end: Same; the system is stated at about 45,000 km across 33 or more countries, designed for up to 180 Tbps on main routes, with most segments expected complete by 2026 (consortium-reported)
note: The 2025-12-01 source's stored date is disputed by its own recapture note, which records a byline of 9 February 2026

subject: infra.connect
name: 5G and aggregate mobile download speeds
